pr.title: Make destructors on `extern "C"` frames to be executed
pr.description:
This would make the example in #123231 print "Noisy Drop". I didn't mark this as fixing the issue because the behaviour is yet to be spec'ed.

Tracking:

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/74990
pr.author: nbdd0121

analysis.originalLogic: In `AbortUnwindingCalls`, MIR basic blocks were processed after an early `if block.is_cleanup { continue; }` guard. For non-cleanup blocks, if a call could unwind and the surrounding body could not unwind, the pass unconditionally rewrote that call's unwind action to `UnwindAction::Terminate(UnwindTerminateReason::Abi)`. This replaced any existing landing-pad action, including `UnwindAction::Cleanup`. Cleanup blocks were skipped entirely, so an `UnwindResume` terminator inside a cleanup block was not converted to termination.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Because `else if !body_can_unwind` rewrote every unwinding call's action to `Terminate`, calls that originally had `UnwindAction::Cleanup` lost their cleanup landing pad. The generated code aborted immediately instead of entering cleanup, so destructors/drops on the non-unwinding (`extern "C"`) frame were not executed. Separately, skipping cleanup blocks left `UnwindResume` unchanged inside them. The corrected transformation only replaces `UnwindAction::Continue` with `Terminate`, preserves `Cleanup` so destructors run, and replaces `UnwindResume` with `UnwindTerminate(Abi)` in all blocks, including cleanup blocks, so termination happens after cleanup.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR for functions whose ABI cannot unwind (e.g. `extern "C"`; `extern "C-unwind"` is filtered out), where a callee can unwind and the frame may have live locals with destructors, producing cleanup landing pads. It also covers cleanup blocks ending in `UnwindResume` and inline asm marked `options(may_unwind)`.
analysis.summary: The AbortUnwindingCalls pass previously replaced a call's unwind action with `Terminate` even when it was `Cleanup`, which bypassed landing pads and prevented destructors on non-unwinding `extern "C"` frames from running. The fix preserves `Cleanup`, runs it, and only then converts the cleanup block's `UnwindResume` into `UnwindTerminate(Abi)`; it also restricts direct replacement to `UnwindAction::Continue`.
analysis.trigger: The function body cannot unwind (`body_can_unwind == false`, e.g. `extern "C"`) and contains either a call that may unwind with `UnwindAction::Cleanup`, or a cleanup block whose terminator is `UnwindResume`.
preconditions: The enclosing function ABI cannot unwind, such as `extern "C"` rather than `extern "C-unwind"`.
A call inside that function may unwind and has a cleanup action because a live local requires Drop.
The cleanup path ends in `UnwindResume`, which must become `UnwindTerminate(Abi)` after cleanup.
Cleanup blocks must be inspected before the `if block.is_cleanup { continue; }` guard.
pitfalls: Do not clobber `UnwindAction::Cleanup` with `Terminate`; doing so skips destructor execution.
Only replace `UnwindAction::Continue` directly; preserve cleanup paths and terminate after they run.
`UnwindResume` inside cleanup blocks must be handled even though cleanup blocks are otherwise skipped.
A direct `terminate(abi)` on the call differs semantically from routing through a cleanup block that finally terminates; the latter permits drops.
Changing this behavior affects existing run-make tests that assumed destructors were skipped across non-unwinding FFI frames.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a mir-opt test with `// EMIT_MIR ... AbortUnwindingCalls.after.mir` and CHECK patterns asserting that a `drop` call has `unwind: [[unwind:bb.*]]`, that the target block is `(cleanup)`, and that it ends with `terminate(abi)`. Add an `extern "C"` function holding a `Drop` value that panics, and a UI run test with `//@ needs-unwind` plus `//@ error-pattern: Noisy Drop` to verify the destructor output is emitted before the abort. Also update asm MAY_UNWIND expectations to route through a cleanup block ending in `terminate(abi)`. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction is claimed.
evidence: Make destructors on `extern "C"` frames to be executed
